correctness.rationale: The arithmetic recurrence follows by appending a bit and gives the four children of the displayed morphism under the stated state labels. The last letters of the greedy arches have their earliest embedding at the successive arch ends, so appending a letter missing from the terminal tail proves the converse to universality. Independent direct scans at levels 0 through 5 give the claimed level-4 rows (counts 4/4/5, 5/5/6, 5/6/5, 4/5/4 with ends O,Z,O,Z) and the odd level-5 rows. Composition reads the right block at the left block's terminal state; substituting the four pairs (0,1),(0,2),(3,1),(3,2) changes the base B to 2(B+1) from even to odd, or 2B−1 from odd to even, and gives the stated offsets and terminal states. At levels 0,1,2,3 the ranges of counts over all inputs are respectively 0–1, 0–1, 1–2, 2–3, all within one of their respective centers. In the binary partition of [0,N), the start of each successive block is divisible by its length, hence each is an aligned substitution block; the incoming states are unrestricted by the per-block bound. Summing the errors proves the claim for all N, including N=1. An independently written arithmetic scan also checked every N through 262144 as finite corroboration, not the proof. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The proof concerns ordinary scattered subsequences of origin-anchored prefixes, not circular subsequences or contiguous factors.
